has: Free File only does this year's taxes. It can't do taxes from past years.

has: If you would rather not do the work yourself, a VITA volunteer can help for free.

Form Filler answer sheet
This is a list of your answers. It is not a tax return. Nothing was sent.

Which free way may fit
Find your income number first
- The IRS calls your income number adjusted gross income, or AGI.
- You can see it by signing in to your IRS online account, under Tax Records.
- You can also ask the IRS to mail you a copy of last year's return.
- Free File was closed when we checked on November 4, 2026. The IRS says it opens in January 2027. Check IRS.gov.
- Always start at IRS.gov/freefile. If you go straight to a tax company's website, you won't get the free deal.
Official link: https://www.irs.gov/freefile
Free help from a VITA volunteer: https://www.irs.gov/individuals/free-tax-return-preparation-for-qualifying-taxpayers or 800-906-9887

Your answers

Was your income $95,000 or less last year? Not answered
Are you willing to type into online copies of the IRS forms yourself? Not answered

Papers to find
[ ] Social Security number or ITIN, for each person on your return
[ ] W-2, the pay form from each job
[ ] 1099 forms, for other money you got
[ ] 1095-A, if you had health insurance from the Marketplace
[ ] Last year's tax return, if you filed one
[ ] IP code the IRS sent you, if any
[ ] Bank account details, if you want your refund sent to your bank
[ ] Papers for credits (if you have them)
[ ] For side jobs: what you were paid, and receipts for what you spent

What you do yourself
- Make your Free File account.
- Check every number on the review page.
- Sign with the income number from last year's return, or a 5-digit code you pick.
- Press Submit, the button that sends your tax return.
- If you owe tax, you pay it yourself.

This tool never presses Submit, signs for you, pays anything, or picks an extra that costs money. It never asks for your Free File password.
If any screen asks for a card number, stop.
Source: IRS Free File page, https://www.irs.gov/filing/irs-free-file-do-your-taxes-for-free
